---
title: "Theme tokens"
subtitle: "The vocabulary a theme is written in, and what each name accepts."
description: "The theme token vocabulary Lanterne validates against, its defaults, and the two reserved namespaces."
---

A theme is a flat dictionary of tokens.
`theme-tokens` returns the canonical defaults with named overrides applied, and `theme-merge` merges a dictionary of overrides into a complete one.
Both validate every key they touch, so an unknown token name or a value of the wrong type fails where it is written rather than where it is read.

```typst
#let base = theme-tokens(bg: rgb("#fbfbfd"), fg: rgb("#1c1c22"))
#let dark = theme-merge(base, (bg: rgb("#1c1c22"), fg: white))
```

## The vocabulary

Read from `src/theme/tokens.typ`.
The colour, typography and geometry groupings are documentation rather than structure: the dictionary is flat, so a theme merges without recursion and a generated theme is one dictionary literal.

| Token | Accepts | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bg` | colour | `white` | The page fill. |
| `fg` | colour | `rgb("#111111")` | The text colour. |
| `accent` | colour | `rgb("#1f5fa9")` | The theme's accent, such as a title band's fill. |
| `accent-fg` | colour | `white` | The text colour on an accent fill. |
| `muted` | colour | `rgb("#6b6b76")` | Secondary text, such as a footer. |
| `border` | colour | `rgb("#d8d8e0")` | Rules and separators. |
| `dim-opacity` | ratio from 0% to 100% | `30%` | The text fill opacity a dimmed region renders at, read by `dim` and `focus`. |
| `font-base` | family name, coverage-scoped entry, or a non-empty array of them | `"Libertinus Serif"` | The body font. |
| `font-heading` | as `font-base` | `"Libertinus Serif"` | The heading font. |
| `size-base` | positive absolute length | `24pt` | The body text size. An `em` value is rejected here, since it would be relative to itself. |
| `scale-ratio` | number of at least 1 | `1.2` | The step between heading sizes, and what `smaller` divides by. |
| `weight-heading` | integer from 100 to 900, or a weight name | `"semibold"` | The heading weight. |
| `leading` | length | `0.75em` | The paragraph leading. |
| `margin` | length | `2cm` | The page margin. |
| `gutter` | non-negative length | `0.6cm` | The space between the regions of a slide. |
| `header-height` | non-negative length | `2cm` | The height of a header region. |
| `footer-height` | non-negative length | `1cm` | The height of a footer region. |
| `stroke-width` | non-negative length | `1pt` | The thickness of a rule or a border. |
| `extra` | dictionary | `(:)` | Tokens of your own. The one key whose contents are not validated. |
| `slots` | dictionary | `(:)` | A theme's renderers, validated against the five slot names. |

: The token vocabulary. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[15,25,15,45]"}

The named weights are `thin`, `extralight`, `light`, `regular`, `medium`, `semibold`, `bold`, `extrabold` and `black`.

A non-negative length may carry an absolute part, a relative part, or both, and each part must be non-negative on its own.
That is stricter than it sounds: `2cm - 1em` is refused, although it resolves to a positive length at every plausible font size.
The two parts are read separately because Typst refuses to compare a mixed length with zero at all, and comparing the whole would replace this message with Typst's own.

The vocabulary grows with the code that reads a token.
The specification names twenty-eight, and the eighteen above are those the package validates and reads today.
The remaining names arrive with the layout and element milestones.

The six colour tokens are a matched set, tuned for the light default.
Each is overridden on its own, so a theme that sets `bg` to a dark fill should set `muted` and `border` as well, or the secondary text and the rules fall below a readable contrast.

## Heading sizes

A heading's size is `size-base` multiplied by `scale-ratio` raised to `max(0, 3 - level)`, so a section title reads as larger than a slide title and both read as larger than the body, and level 3 and below sit at the base size.

On a slide set `smaller`, the base of that calculation is the slide's own reduced size, so the title shrinks with the body rather than staying as large on the slide that asked for room.

## Light and dark

A theme is one token dictionary, or a pair of them:

```typst
#let paper = (
  light: theme-tokens(bg: white, fg: rgb("#1c1c22")),
  dark: theme-tokens(bg: rgb("#1c1c22"), fg: white),
)

#show: deck.with(theme: paper, theme-mode: "dark")
```

A preset goes in a half like any other token set, so a deck adopts one for each mode:

```typst
#let paired = (
  light: theme-banded(),
  dark: theme-banded(bg: rgb("#1c1c22"), fg: white, muted: rgb("#9a9aa4"), border: rgb("#3a3a44")),
)
```

Neither built in theme ships a dark half of its own: `accent-fg` over `accent` survives a dark background, and `muted` and `border` are tuned for a light one, so a dark deck sets those two.

`theme-mode` takes `"light"` or `"dark"`, and defaults to `"light"`.
A pair is written out; there is no constructor for one.
It carries those two keys and nothing else, so a token written beside them is refused rather than belonging to neither half.

Both halves are validated whichever one renders.
A deck rendered light would otherwise carry a dark half nobody had checked, and the mistake would surface for whoever first rendered it the other way.

What a slide receives is one token dictionary, so nothing downstream knows a pair existed.

Naming a mode against a single token set is not an error: the option says which half to take, and a theme with no halves has one answer.
That answer is the light one, whatever the mode says, so chrome that reads the mode does not draw a dark treatment over light tokens.
If a deck renders light although it names `theme-mode: "dark"`, its theme is a single token dictionary rather than a pair.
That is the one mistake this rule makes quiet, and Typst gives a package no way to warn about it.

A pair is merged one half at a time, because a token belongs to a half rather than to the pair:

```typst
#let louder = (
  light: theme-merge(paper.light, (accent: red)),
  dark: paper.dark,
)
```

## The `extra` namespace

`extra` exists so that a token of your own has somewhere to live.
The strictness everywhere else is the point: a mistyped token name that is quietly ignored is how a theme rots.

`extra` merges key by key rather than replacing wholesale, so setting one token of your own leaves the rest of the base theme's in place.
It is not itself a token name, so `theme-tokens(extra: ...)` is accepted as a key while an unknown name inside the vocabulary is refused.

## The `slots` namespace

`slots` holds a theme's renderers.
It is the second reserved key, and like `extra` it is not a token name and merges key by key, so overriding one colour of a theme does not drop the renderers it supplied.

Unlike `extra`, its contents are validated.
A key must be one of `render-title-slide`, `render-section-slide`, `render-header`, `render-footer` or `render-progress`.
The set of five is fixed, and expanding it is a deliberate versioned decision.
A name outside it is refused rather than stored, because the renderer calls the five it knows and a sixth would be a function nothing ever runs.

Each slot is called with the named arguments `info`, `tokens` and `state`, and returns content.
Write all three, even where the slot ignores one.
Typst exposes nothing of a closure's parameters, so a slot's arity cannot be validated when you write it: one that does not accept all three fails when a page is composed, with Typst's own message rather than this package's.

```typst
#let banded = theme-tokens(
  accent: rgb("#1f5fa9"),
  accent-fg: white,
  slots: (
    render-header: (info: none, tokens: none, state: none) => {
      // A slide opened by `#pagebreak()` has no title, so the header says there
      // is no region on that page rather than placing nothing.
      if state.title == none { return none }
      block(
        width: 100%,
        height: 100%,
        fill: tokens.accent,
        inset: 1em,
        text(fill: tokens.accent-fg, state.title),
      )
    },
  ),
)
```

## The built in themes

Two, and a deck names one or neither.

```typst
#import "@preview/lanterne:0.1.0": *

#show: deck.with(theme: theme-banded(accent: rgb("#1f5fa9")))
```

`theme-plain` is the canonical defaults and no renderers, so a slide is its title and its body on a dressed page.
It is what a deck renders under when it names no theme, and `theme-default` returns it.
A default that draws chrome would be a default every deck had to opt out of.

`theme-banded` composes: the title goes in a coloured band, a rule and the deck's own title run along the foot, and a section slide gives the band up for a page of its own.
Its renderers read `accent` and `accent-fg` for the band, `muted`, `border` and `stroke-width` for the footer rule, and `gutter` and the two region heights for their padding.

A section slide is composed by one slot, so it carries no footer.
A whole-page slot replaces every region, not only the body.

Neither built in theme opens a title page.
A deck that wants one supplies `render-title-slide` itself, merged into whichever preset it adopts.

Both take named overrides, exactly as `theme-tokens` does, so a deck adopts one and changes what it likes:

```typst
#show: deck.with(theme: theme-banded(accent: red, font-base: "Inter"))
```

Overriding a colour keeps the renderers, since `slots` merges key by key.
To take a theme's chrome without one part, clear that slot:

```typst
#let quiet = theme-merge(theme-banded(), (slots: (render-footer: none)))
```

## What a slot composes

Two of the five compose a whole page, and three fill a region of one.

| Slot | Composes |
| --- | --- |
| `render-title-slide` | A page of its own, before the first slide, from the deck's `info`. |
| `render-section-slide` | The whole page of a section slide, in place of the centred default. |
| `render-header` | The region above the body of a content slide. |
| `render-progress` | A region below the body. |
| `render-footer` | The region at the foot of a content slide. |

: The five slots. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

A region with no slot behind it takes no space at all, so a theme supplying none composes the page exactly as a themeless deck does.
A slot may also return `none` to say that its region takes no space on this page, which is how a theme hides its footer on an appendix slide or its progress bar on the first step.
A slot that was handed the slide's title may not decline, since declining would leave the title nowhere: that is refused with a message naming the slot and the slide.
Blank content is refused for the same reason and by the same message, because it loses the title just as completely.

`render-title-slide` reads both differently: `none`, or content with nothing on it, means the deck has no title page, and none is emitted.
That is how a theme writes a title page conditional on the metadata it is given, whether the conditional is written in code or in markup.

A section slide uses its own slot and carries no header, footer or progress region.
A title slide is a page of its own and carries none either: it is not a slide of the deck, so the deck's chrome does not belong on it.

::: {.callout-warning}

## A header slot must place the title

Supplying `render-header` moves the title out of the body, so the header is the only place it can appear.
A header that ignores `state.title` deletes the title from the slide, from the outline and from the PDF bookmarks.
If the slide was labelled, the label goes with the heading, and a reference to that slide then fails to compile with a Typst message naming neither the theme nor the slot.

Place `state.title` somewhere, or supply no header slot and let the title render in the body.
:::

Every region is as tall as what it holds, and the body takes the rest of the page.
A region asks for its height where it is drawn: the built in themes read `header-height` and `footer-height` as the padding around one line, so a band holding one line comes to about that height and one holding two comes to more.

A region sized by a fixed row was the first shape and it was wrong twice.
A slide title long enough to wrap had its second line cut through the middle of the glyphs, and a theme given `header-height: 0` lost the title altogether, because the title had already been taken out of the body to be put in a band with no room in it.
Sized by its content, a long title grows its band and moves the body down, which is a page a reader can still read.

Suppress a region by clearing its slot rather than by giving it no height.
`header-height: 0` gives a band with no padding, not the absence of one.

The region heights are deck-level and do not shrink under `slide-options(smaller: true)`, which shrinks the text: a region that shrank with it would put one slide's chrome out of line with the rest of the deck.

Regions render in the flow of the page rather than in Typst's own page header.
That is what keeps a title placed in one numbered, restyled by your own rules, listed in the outline and reachable by a reference.

## What a slot receives

`state` describes the page being composed.

| Key | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"section"`, `"content"`, or `"title"` on the deck's title page. |
| `title` | The slide's title as content you can place, or `none`. |
| `title-source` | `"heading"`, `"value"`, or `none`. |
| `level` | The heading level the title stands at, or `none`. |
| `appendix` | Whether the slide is an appendix slide. |
| `body` | The slide's content, with the title removed when it was taken out. |
| `step` | `(index: ..., total: ...)`, one-based, over the slide's whole step space. |
| `mode` | `"light"` or `"dark"`. |

: What `state` carries. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[25,75]"}

`title` is content only when this page has somewhere to put it: a header slot on a content slide, or the section slot on a section slide.
A slot that is handed one has to place it, whichever source it came from.
A theme that places no title leaves it in the body where it was written, because taking it out with nowhere to put it would delete it from the slide.

`title-source` says what kind of thing `title` is.
`"heading"` is the heading you wrote, carried out of the body with the style rules in force over it, so your own `show heading` rule reaches it.
`"value"` is what was passed to `slide(title: ...)`, which is not a heading at all, so no such rule reaches it.
A theme that wants the two to look alike sets the font and size itself rather than wrapping the value in `heading(...)`, which would add a second heading to the document and put an explicit slide in the outline.

`step` counts over the slide's whole step space rather than over the pages this render emits, so a handout reports the step it kept.

`state` describes the slide, not the deck.
There is no slide index, slide total or page position in it yet, so a progress bar over the whole deck and a slide number are not yet expressible: they arrive with the `progress` and `slide-number` tokens in a later release.

A value of `none` clears a slot rather than storing one.
That is how a theme takes another's chrome without one of its parts, since every other value has to be a function.

```typst
#let quiet = theme-merge(banded, (slots: (render-header: none)))
```
